critique.evidence: The dark editorial system, restrained cyan/green accents, strong headline, crisp borders, and consistent mono labels create a polished, coherent identity. Desktop hierarchy is especially clear. However, tablet and mobile become excessively tall and repetitive; mobile metadata and header navigation are extremely small and low-contrast, with the header visibly truncating labels. The mobile precedent rows also lose the efficient horizontal relationship between item, status, and similarity, weakening scanability. Serious contrast checks remain incomplete for 12 mobile header nodes and one tablet node, so top-tier polish is not proven.
critique.fix: Increase small-text size and contrast, give the active header item a clearly persistent state, and replace the clipped mobile navigation with a more legible compact pattern. On mobile, condense each precedent into a tighter two-column row with similarity aligned opposite the item details, reducing vertical repetition while preserving hierarchy.
